stem: Headaches: Researchers are interested in testing a new treatment for migraine headaches. They want to find the proportion of all migraine sufferers who would benefit from the new drug. They conduct a study in 2024 by taking a sample of 200 migraine sufferers seeking treatment in Los Angeles, California and give them the new drug to use for 2 months.
prompt: Try each one, then compare with the sample answers.
items: Identify the population | Identify the sample | Identify the parameter of interest | Identify the statistic
answer: All migraine sufferers. | The 200 migraine sufferers in Los Angeles who were given the new drug. | The proportion of all migraine sufferers who would benefit from the new drug. | The proportion of the 200 sampled migraine sufferers who benefited from the new drug.

prompt: The school district is considering whether it will no longer allow students to park at school after two recent accidents where students were severely injured. As a first step, they survey parents of high school students by mail, asking them whether or not the parents would object to this policy change. Of 5,799 surveys that go out, 1,209 are returned. Of these 1,209 surveys that were completed, 926 agreed with the policy change and 283 disagreed. Which of the following statements is true?
options: The survey is unlikely to have any bias because all parents were mailed a survey. | The school district has strong support from parents to move forward with the policy approval. | It is possible that 80% of the parents of high school students agree with the policy change. | Because many surveys have return rates of between 30% and 50%, it is likely that some of the mailings never reached the parents.
explanation: Only about 21% of the surveys came back. The parents who replied may not represent all parents, so a true agreement of 80% is possible.

prompt: Two statistics students at UCLA conducted an energy efficiency survey of graduate student apartments. There were seven university apartment buildings, and the students randomly selected three to be included in the study. In each building, they randomly chose 25 apartments. What is the largest group of students that the study results represent?
options: All UCLA graduate student apartments. | All UCLA graduate student apartments in this group of seven buildings. | All UCLA graduate student apartments in the three sampled buildings. | All UCLA graduate student apartments that were sampled in the three buildings.
explanation: The three buildings were randomly chosen from the seven. The results can be generalized to those seven buildings, not to all of UCLA.

prompt: A city council has requested a household survey be conducted in a suburban area of their city. The area is broken into many distinct and unique neighborhoods, some including large homes, some with only apartments, and others a diverse mixture of housing structures. Which approach would likely be the least effective?
options: Cluster sampling: randomly pick 3 unique neighborhoods to go to and survey all 1000 homes in those neighborhoods. | Stratified sampling: randomly pick 200 large homes to survey, 350 apartments to survey, and 450 from the diverse housing structures. | Simple random sampling: include all addresses in a computer program, use a random number generator to select 1000 homes to go to.
explanation: Only 3 neighborhoods could miss the variety across the area. The other two approaches reach every kind of housing.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of stratified sampling?
options: A sample of 351 people called a radio show to express their opinions about the verdict in the Michael Jackson trial. | In order to assess students' satisfaction with the food establishment on campus, the first 50 students that come out of the student center were interviewed. | A poll asked a random sample of 1,112 adults whether they believe that the use of marijuana for medical reasons should be legalized. | A health educator wanted to study the sleeping habits of the undergraduate students in her university. For her study, the researcher chose a simple random sample of size 150 from each of the classes (150 freshmen, 150 sophomores, 150 juniors, and 150 seniors), for a total of 600 sampled students. | The human resources department of a large bank wanted to assess the job satisfaction of the bank's workers. The department chose four of the bank's branches at random, and used all of the workers in those four branches as the subjects for the study.
explanation: Stratified sampling splits the population into groups, then samples within each group. Here the groups are the four classes.

prompt: Which of the variables are categorical and which are quantitative?
options: Categorical: Name, Phone number. Quantitative: Years Volunteering, Number of siblings, Annual income. | Categorical: Name. Quantitative: Years Volunteering, Phone number, Number of siblings, Annual income. | Categorical: Name, Phone number, Number of Siblings. Quantitative: Years Volunteering, Annual income. | All are categorical. None are quantitative.
explanation: A phone number names a person. It is not a quantity, and averaging phone numbers would mean nothing.

stem: The following graph was presented in a New York Times Opinion article from 2019. Look at the graph labeled "Free college for all students". It shows the relationship between two variables: support for free college for all students, and age.
prompt: Describe the association between these two variables.
answer: Support is highest for the youngest group, ages 18 to 29, and tends to be lower in each older group. The groups under 50 are above the 57% average, and the 50 to 64 and 65+ groups are below it. A good answer names the direction and uses groups or numbers from the graph.
